summary: This Snowflake documentation page summarizes the categories of functions the platform supports. It says Snowflake supports most standard SQL:1999 functions and parts of the SQL:2003 analytic extensions. It briefly describes scalar, aggregate, window, table, system, user-defined (UDF) and external functions, with links to fuller lists.
one_line: Snowflake documentation summarizing its function categories: scalar, aggregate, window, table, system, user-defined and external functions.
key_facts: Snowflake supports most of the standard functions defined in SQL:1999.
Snowflake supports parts of the SQL:2003 analytic extensions.
A scalar function returns one value per invocation, which in most cases can be thought of as one value per row.
Aggregate functions in Snowflake operate on values across rows to perform calculations such as sum, average, counting, minimum/maximum values, standard deviation, and estimation.
Aggregate functions also support some non-mathematical operations.
Window functions operate on a subset of rows within the set of input rows.
Table functions provide information about Snowflake features and services.
A complete summary of table functions is available at List of System-Defined Table Functions.
System functions are provided by Snowflake as system-defined functions.
In addition to system-defined functions, users can create their own functions in Snowflake.
Snowflake supports user-defined functions (UDFs) as a type of user-created function.
External functions are functions which are stored and executed outside Snowflake.
The page lists seven sections: Scalar Functions, Aggregate Functions, Window Functions, Table Functions, System Functions, User-defined Functions (UDFs), and External Functions.
